A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete, readable 21-page paper, LEDOM: Reverse Language Model, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the research content matches; visible differences are confined to the first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original LEDOM benchmark evaluations and Reverse Reward experiments in Tables 3–4, training and sampling-size analyses, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains the same original benchmark results, Reverse Reward experiments, training analyses, and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: The reverse-token training procedure, 2B/7B architectures, bidirectional scoring, response reranking, and step-wise beam search are identical in Sections 2 and 5 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DCLM/MAP-Neo pretraining data, OpenMathInstruct-2 fine-tuning data, benchmark coverage in Tables 3–4, and qualitative test scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same matched FLMs, DeepSeekMath, QwenMath, and OpenMath2 models, with unchanged participation of greedy decoding, random selection, and forward-scored candidates.

E3.justification: Few-shot prompting, token reversal, accuracy/Pass@1 metrics, training budgets, and inference settings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. No evaluation procedure is added or revised.

E4.justification: The sampling-size analysis in Figure 3, training dynamics in Figure 4, behavioral examples, and mathematical case studies in Tables 7–8 are identical.

E5.justification: Appendix D.2.2 specifies the same fine-tuning seed of 0. Both versions retain the same reporting practices, without repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted curves, and qualitative outputs match throughout. For example, Table 4 retains QwenMath with Reverse Reward at 80.8% on MATH-500 and 96.1% on GSM8K in both versions.

T1.justification: The factorization definitions, entropy identity, Bayesian scoring derivation, Proposition 1 and its proof, and appendix mathematics are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion make identical claims about LEDOM's scale, reverse-generation capabilities, posterior verification, and mathematical-reasoning gains.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of directional complementarity and posterior degradation, beam-search failure discussion, and limitations concerning scale, task asymmetry, posterior quality, verification baselines, and safety.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, prompting instructions, and resource-release statements are identical. Embedded external link targets also match apart from the paper's own arXiv version link.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to TRLM and earlier bidirectional, reverse-generation, and alternative token-ordering work.

P1.justification: Only the arXiv stamp text changes from v3, dated 3 Mar 2026, to v4, dated 25 Jul 2026. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp is repositioned and slightly reformatted. Figures 1–6, Tables 1–8, and the remaining layout are unchanged; pages 2–21 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, results, explanations, reproducibility information, and appendices are identical. Updating and repositioning the arXiv stamp does not meaningfully affect readability, evidential support, or overall paper quality.
